rules:
# goal: how the reminders work

- A reminder comes when all of these hold: no letter waits in your queue, your last message is an answer with no tool call (or your conversation is still empty: then the goal is your first message), and the goal is `active`.
- Each reminder is one more message in your history; keep the goal text short.
- Progress: if you call any tool other than `goal` after a reminder, the count starts again at 0. Only talking, or calling `goal` with op get, does not count.
- Limit: after `limit` reminders in a row without progress (default 10) you get one last message `[aos] goal: reminder limit 10 reached; goal paused ...` and the goal is `paused`. `resume` starts it again from 0.
- `done`: only when the goal is really finished (`status` done) or cannot be done (`status` abandoned). Give one sentence why. No more reminders after it; `set` gives a new goal.
- `pause`: when you cannot go on for now: you wait for an answer, a person, or another agent. Give one sentence why. A letter does not resume it: call `resume` yourself when you can go on.
- The goal lives in your stack (`goal.json`), not in your history: it stays when your history is summarized.
errors:
# goal: errors

- `GoalMissing`: you have no goal. `set` one first, or do nothing.
- `GoalEnded`: the goal is done or abandoned, so it cannot be paused or resumed. `set` a new one if there is more to do.
- `GoalBad`: the goal file in your stack is broken. `set` writes it again.
- `WriteFailed`: the goal file could not be written (disk, rights). Report it.
- `DaemonMissing`, `InstanceMissing`: you are not running under a daemon, so the tool cannot find you. Report it.
- `ArgumentsBad`, `OpUnknown`: op is one of get, set, done, pause, resume; set needs `text`; done and pause need `reason`; `limit` is a whole number of at least 1. See `aos/errors/common.json#/input`.
